options.text: Managed guest session
Device

USB

questions.question: You have been asked to describe ChromeOS’s built-in security features. What benefit does enabling Verified Boot provide on a ChromeOS device?

options.text: It ensures that the OS is uncompromised
It allows updates to happen in the background
Running both operating systems on one device at the same time makes it twice as powerful
It installs the known safe backup OS every time the device is started up

questions.explanation: Verified Boot validates the ChromeOS operating system during startup, helping ensure that the OS has not been compromised or tampered with.

questions.question:
An administrator wants to use a custom extension to install a client certificate on a ChromeOS device so it can connect to the corporate Wi-Fi.  
  
Which action is required to achieve this?

options.text: Install on the device via guest mode
Distribute through the Chrome Web Store
Force-install to the device
Encode the certificate in DER-encoded format

questions.explanation:
Extensions that provision client certificates through the ChromeOS enterprise platform keys API must be force-installed by policy; the API is available only to force-installed extensions. [Manage client certificates on ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6080885?hl=en)\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage client certificates on ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6080885?hl=en)

questions.question: You need to configure a policy that stops the device from shutting down when it is idle at the sign-in screen. Where should you go?

options.text: User Settings > Idle settings
User Settings > User Experience
Device Settings > Allow shutdown
Device Settings > Power management

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS device Power management settings configure sleep or shutdown behavior at the sign-in screen and can be used to ensure kiosk-style devices do not shut down. The Allow shutdown setting only controls how users can manually power off a device.\
\
**Learn more:** [Set ChromeOS device policies](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1375678?hl=en)

questions.question: You have been asked to select a third-party IdP to enable sign-in to ChromeOS devices. Your ChromeOS devices display an **"Unable to sign in to Google"** message. How should you troubleshoot this?

options.text: Ensure the identity provider is using an SAML compliant connection
Check Multi-Factor Authentication for the user account in the Google Admin console
Disable the SSO connection in the Google Admin console
Apply the SSO certificate to the ChromeOS device

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS device sign-in through a third-party identity provider requires SAML-based SSO, with the domain configured for SAML SSO and an SP-initiated SAML flow. Verifying that the identity provider uses a compatible SAML connection addresses a failure to redirect and authenticate through the IdP.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure SAML single sign-on for ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6060880?hl=en)

questions.question: You have been asked to select a third-party IdP to enable sign-in to ChromeOS devices. Your ChromeOS devices display an **"Unable to sign in to Google"** message. How should you troubleshoot this?

You are configuring a proof of concept in an email-verified trial environment instead of a domain-verified environment. When you attempt to integrate the existing third-party Identity Provider (IdP) to provision user accounts, an error occurs. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: You need to purchase Google Workspace licenses to be able to integrate with third party IdPs.
You are only able to manage devices in an email-verified domain, not users.
Email-verified domain environments only allow for a single managed user per domain.
You need to verify a domain in order to integrate with third party IdPs.

questions.explanation:
A domain must be verified before Google can enable the organization-level identity-management features needed to manage and provision user accounts through a third-party IdP. Domain verification proves ownership of the business identity and unlocks full administrative control of user accounts.

**Learn more:** [Verify your domain to unlock features (for business email accounts)](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9122284?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You rely on a number of applications and want to ensure they continue to run smoothly with every new version of Chrome. What should you do?

options.text: Ask users to provide feedback on the applications within a week of a new Chrome release.
Advise them to take no action. All applications are automatically supported on the latest version of Chrome.
Always install the latest version of those applications when they become available so they are always compatible with the latest version of Chrome.
Implement a QA strategy and put their IT group and 5% of users on the beta channel of ChromeOS so they can find and report bugs early for upcoming Chrome releases.

questions.explanation:
A quality-assurance strategy that places IT staff and a small representative group of users on the ChromeOS Beta channel exposes application compatibility issues before the Stable release reaches the wider organization. Google recommends keeping at least 5% of devices on Beta so organizations can identify and report problems early and, if needed, block an update before broad deployment.

**Learn more:** [ChromeOS release best practices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6025002?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization’s security protocols require that users are logged out of any unattended devices after 24 hours. You can remotely access each device and sign out of the user account using Chrome Remote Desktop
Force-install a custom app to each device in question that notifies the user that they need to sign out of their device after 24 hours

The ChromeOS **Maximum user session length** policy centrally controls the duration of user sessions and automatically signs users out when that duration expires. It accepts values from 1 to 1,440 minutes (24 hours), so configuring it for 24 hours enforces the required limit at scale.

**Learn more:** [Set Chrome policies for users or browsers](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289?hl=en)

**Learn more:** [Manage updates on ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/3168106?hl=en)

questions.question:
A super admin is configuring third-party SSO for their organization. When testing with their own account, they do not see the SSO screen.  
  
What is responsible for this behavior?

options.text: SSO settings are misconfigured
The account is in the wrong OrgUnit
Third-party SSO is not enabled
Super admin bypassed the third-party

Google Workspace super administrators bypass third-party SSO when signing in to the Admin console, so they can retain direct administrative access. Google does not redirect them to the SSO sign-in page.\

With the business unit scoped to its own organizational unit (OU), force the installation of the app and extension to your users and browsers via the URL of the web application.

questions.question: An organization has created organizational units in the Google Admin console to provide additional management structure. What is the most effective way to manage each OU without affecting the top-level OU policy?

options.text: Delete sublevel OUs and only work from the top level OU
Disable auto updates
Override the inheritance for a given policy
Force inheritance from top level OU to all OUs

questions.explanation:
Organizational units inherit policies from their parent by default. Overriding a specific policy at a child OU applies a local setting while leaving the top-level OU policy unchanged. [Set Chrome policies for users or browsers](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/2657289?hl=en)\
\

questions.question: An organization has created organizational units in the Google Admin console to provide additional management structure. What is the most effective way to manage each OU without affecting the top-level OU policy?

options.text: In the “Digital Signage” child organization, disable scheduled reboots except on Friday.
In the “Digital Signage” child organization, set the policy to always reboot on Friday on user sign-out.
In the “Digital Signage” child organization, apply reboot after the uptime limit on Friday.
In the “Digital Signage” child organization, set the policy to enable scheduled reboots on Friday.

The ChromeOS Scheduled reboot device policy lets an administrator specify the reboot time, frequency (including weekly), and day of the week. Enabling that scheduled-reboot policy for Friday in the Digital Signage organizational unit applies the weekly Friday reboot configuration to the devices in that unit.

questions.question: How can you use Chrome Remote Desktop from the Google Admin console to connect to a user?

options.text: Find the user account and click remote desktop
Open Chrome Remote Desktop and type the device serial number
Open Chrome Remote Desktop and type the user's username
Find the device and click remote desktop

Google Admin console remote support is initiated by locating the managed ChromeOS device under **Devices > Chrome > Devices**, opening that device’s details, and selecting **Remote Desktop**. The session connects to the device currently used by the user.\
\
**Learn more:** [Remotely connect to ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9547497?hl=en)

questions.question: After deploying your Android VPN client, you want to enforce an always-on VPN. Where do you configure it?

options.text: Device settings - Always-on VPN
via JSON configuration with the deployed application
Network settings - Always-on VPN
User settings - Always-on VPN

questions.explanation:
Always-on VPN is configured in Android Enterprise device settings under the Connectivity section. This device-level policy selects a supported VPN client and makes it automatically connect and reconnect; the VPN client’s JSON app configuration is used for its connection-specific settings instead.\
\
**Learn more:** [Device restriction settings for Android in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-configuration/templates/ref-device-restrictions-android-enterprise) · [Use VPN settings for Android Enterprise in Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configuration/vpn-settings-android-enterprise)

questions.question: Which two methods can customers use to open a support case for ChromeOS? (Choose two.)

options.text: Chat support via the Admin console
Contact the device manufacturer
File feedback on the device with Alt + Shift + i
File case through Customer Care Portal
Send an email to ChromeOS support

questions.explanation:
Eligible ChromeOS administrators can contact Google support through the Admin console, and the Customer Care Portal supports submitting and managing support cases. Device feedback, hardware-manufacturer contact, and a general support email do not constitute the designated formal Google support-case channels.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get support — Chrome Enterprise and Education Help](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/4594885?hl=en) · [Google Workspace reseller access to the Customer Care Portal](https://support.google.com/channelservices/answer/11198038?hl=en)

questions.question: How can a ChromeOS administrator capture logs remotely?

options.text: Enable device system log upload device settings
Find the user and click Capture logs
Enable user log upload in user settings
Find the device and click Capture logs

questions.explanation:
In the Google Admin console, the **Capture logs** action on an individual ChromeOS device triggers a new upload of that device’s attributes and logs. Device system log upload must be enabled beforehand, but it is a prerequisite rather than the action that initiates an on-demand capture.\
\
**Learn more:** [View ChromeOS device list and details](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333?hl=en)

questions.question: How can a ChromeOS administrator capture logs remotely?

ChromeOS is installed with the previous organization’s custom image

Forced re-enrollment causes a wiped ChromeOS device to automatically enroll back into the organization that previously managed it. A prior owner must deprovision a device to completely remove that administrative control before it can be successfully enrolled in another organization.

**Learn more:** [Force wiped ChromeOS devices to re-enroll](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6352858?hl=en) · [Buying and selling previously managed ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16971717?hl=en)

options.text: Every time ChromeOS updates, it automatically updates the antivirus software on the device

Canary

questions.question:
A user is having unusual problems in which their device shows a distorted image on the screen.  
  
What is the first action they can take that might resolve the issue?

Run a virus scan
Reinstall the operating system

questions.question: You want to enterprise-enroll a device that has already been signed in to. What should you do first?

options.text: Delete all consumer accounts, and then follow the same steps for enrolling a brand new device
Follow the same steps for enrolling a brand new device
Contact Google support to convert the device into an enterprise device.
Wipe the device.

A ChromeOS device must be enrolled before any user signs in. If a user has already signed in, wiping the device resets it so enterprise enrollment can begin correctly.\

questions.question: What should an administrator do to see the number and type of ChromeOS upgrades that their domain has purchased and is using?

Check subscriptions in billing
Contact partner to verify
Check reports page for upgrades

The Admin console’s **Devices > Chrome > Devices > Upgrades** view displays upgrade types and totals, including purchased standalone upgrades and assigned (in-use) upgrades.\

What is the best option an administrator can use to investigate this issue?

Review using remote desktop
Change the device resolution
Change the device policy

questions.question:
A large bank needs all its ChromeOS devices to automatically connect to its managed SSIDs.

Install a firewall on each ChromeOS device

Create a ChromeOS Developer Account

ChromeOS Flex

questions.question: A customer runs a mission-critical workload on ChromeOS and needs devices configured to reduce ChromeOS changes. Add an update rollout plan

questions.question: When ChromeOS devices have several auto-connect networks configured, which of the following rules applies to determine which network is used?

Networks prefer unmanaged networks configured by the user over managed networks set by policy

You are partnering with a customer to reduce electronic waste, prolong hardware lifecycles, and pursue environmentally responsible initiatives. ChromeOS Flex (Beta) has been identified as a possible solution to address these areas.  
  
What considerations must you make when deploying ChromeOS Flex (Beta)?

options.text: Security, apps, hardware, and management of devices will need to be vetted for functionality and feature parity.
All hardware capable of installing an operating system is in scope for this solution.
UL Energy Efficiency certification denotes environmental standards to be leveraged upon deployment of ChromeOS Flex (Beta).
ChromeOS Flex (Beta) requires the least amount of device testing and can therefore exepdite production readiness.

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS Flex deployment requires vetting device hardware and functionality, security configuration, application support, and management capabilities. Google guarantees functionality only for certified models, documents feature differences from ChromeOS, and recommends deployment-specific security measures such as Secure Boot and TPM configuration.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for installation — ChromeOS Flex Help](https://support.google.com/chromeosflex/answer/11552529) · [Differences between ChromeOS Flex and ChromeOS — ChromeOS Flex Help](https://support.google.com/chromeosflex/answer/11542901)

questions.question: Which management capability makes ChromeOS devices a popular option for IT administrators in educational institutions and enterprises?

options.text: Secure management through on prem infrastructure
Remote BIOS controls and firmware update
Centralized management through Admin console
Inability to remotely control and monitor devices

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS supports centralized cloud management through the Google Admin console, allowing administrators to apply policies and manage ChromeOS devices across an organization from one place.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get started with Chrome & ChromeOS device management](https://support.google.com/a/answer/13801455?hl=en)

questions.question: You need to reduce the likelihood of a breach involving your organization’s identities. What should you do to minimize that risk?

options.text: Configure individual Google Accounts
Set up Single Sign-on (SSO)
Set up Client-side encryption
Connect your LDAP

questions.explanation:
Single sign-on (SSO) centralizes user authentication with an identity provider, reducing the number of separate credentials and enabling consistent application of access and authentication controls across services.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage single sign-on (SSO) with Microsoft accounts](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/12498137?hl=en)

questions.question: When configuring a Chrome Enterprise trial, what is one benefit of electing to verify the domain?

options.text: Identity management
Application management
Network management
Device management

questions.explanation:
Verifying the organization’s domain unlocks identity-management features by confirming domain ownership. This enables administrative control over user accounts, profiles, and security settings; domain-verified Chrome Enterprise accounts also support custom roles and granular privileges.\
\
**Learn more:** [Verify your domain to unlock features](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9122284?hl=en) · [About email-verified and domain-verified accounts](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/10435184?hl=en)

questions.question: You need to access the enterprise enrollment screen. What should you do?

options.text: Press Ctrl-Alt-E during the Chrome bootup sequence (Chrome logo animation)
Sign in with enterprise enrollment credentials provided by the customer at the user sign-in screen
Press Ctrl-Alt-E on the initial welcome screen to set initial settings
Press Ctrl-Alt-E at the user login screen before any user has signed in to the device

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS devices must be enrolled before any user signs in. If the enrollment prompt does not appear, pressing Ctrl+Alt+E at the user login screen opens the enterprise enrollment flow. Google Chrome Enterprise documentation specifies this shortcut must be used before anyone signs in.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enroll ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1360534?hl=en-GB)

questions.question: The IT team configured a policy that lets users reset (powerwash) their device to its default state. The team wants to ensure the devices remain fully managed at all times. What should you do to accomplish this goal?

options.text: Set the \
Set the “Sign-in Restriction” policy to “Allow any user to sign-in”
Set the “Single Sign-On IdP redirection” policy to “Allow users to go directly to SAML SSO IdP page”
Set the “Forced re-enrollment” policy to “Force device to automatically re-enroll after wiping”

questions.explanation:
Setting Forced re-enrollment to automatically re-enroll the device after wiping causes a wiped ChromeOS device to re-enroll into the organization, preserving management and enforcement of device policies after a powerwash.\
\
**Learn more:** [Force wiped ChromeOS devices to re-enroll](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6352858?hl=en)

questions.question:
A large pharmaceutical company enrolls in a Chrome trial and wants to purchase Chrome licenses. An administrator must verify the domain.  
  
How can an administrator verify the domain in the Admin console?

options.text: Contact Google support and give them the MX record
Call the DNS provider and give them an NS record
Add the TXT record to the DNS setting at their domain registrar
Ask the network administrator to approve the DNS record

questions.explanation:
Domain ownership is verified by copying the unique TXT record supplied in the Google Admin console, adding it to the domain’s DNS settings at the domain registrar or DNS host, and confirming the record in the Admin console.\
\
**Learn more:** [Verify your domain with a TXT record](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6169597?hl=en-sg)

questions.question: When using certificates with SCEP, where should an administrator install the Google Cloud Certificate Connector?

options.text: On a Windows server connected to the network
Downloads folder of the
Root partition of the ChromeOS device
Install to the Google Cloud App Engine

questions.explanation:
The Google Cloud Certificate Connector is a Windows service that securely connects Google to an on-premises CA/SCEP infrastructure. It must be installed on the CA server or on a Windows machine that can reach that server across the network.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use the Google Cloud Certificate Connector](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/11053129?hl=en)

questions.question: At any one time, how many copies of ChromeOS does a ChromeOS device keep?
questions.explanation:
ChromeOS maintains two system images in an A/B partition layout: the active image and an alternate image used to install updates and provide rollback if the active image cannot boot.\
\
**Learn more:** [Chromium OS File System and Autoupdate](https://www.chromium.org/chromium-os/chromiumos-design-docs/filesystem-autoupdate/)

questions.question: To place a device in kiosk mode, which setting must be enabled in **Apps & extensions**?

options.text: Set auto-launch app to the app to be used
Select the correct group when adding the app
Pin the version to the latest version
Select the correct OU when adding the app

questions.explanation:
A ChromeOS device operates as a single-purpose kiosk when a kiosk app is configured to launch automatically. In the Admin console’s Apps & extensions > Kiosks settings, select the intended app as the Auto-launch app.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Chrome kiosk app settings](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9273974?hl=en-EN)

questions.question: To place a device in kiosk mode, which setting must be enabled in **Apps & extensions**?

options.text: Setup “Managed Browser
Enable “User Session” settings
Configure “Managed Guest Session
Implement “Kiosk Mode

questions.explanation:
Managed guest sessions provide a policy-managed, shared ChromeOS session in which administrators can configure Chrome Browser behavior and manage applications. By contrast, Kiosk Mode runs a single Chrome or Android app, so it does not satisfy a requirement for both a managed browser and a separate custom application.

**Learn more:** [Managed guest session devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/3017014?hl=en) · [Launching the Kiosk Mode app on ChromeOS devices](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/14839581?hl=en)

questions.question: Your team includes members who work remotely. Your CTO wants to ensure that the fleet of ChromeOS devices remains managed by corporate policy even after a device wipe. What should you configure to meet this objective?

options.text: Create strict password rules
Edit the setting “Verified Access\
Set the setting “Powerwash’’ to “Do not allow powerwash to be triggered”
Set up the Admin console to force the device to automatically re-enroll after wiping

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS Forced re-enrollment can be configured to force a device to automatically re-enroll after wiping. This returns the wiped device to the organization’s management so its corporate policies continue to be enforced.\
\
**Learn more:** [Force wiped ChromeOS devices to re-enroll](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/6352858?hl=en)

options.text: From the “Device information” page, check the “Device Type” attribute content.
Check your “Billing subscription” page to identify devices with CBE and CEU.
Check directly from the device through the “About Chrome OS” page.
Check from the device through chrome://policy

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS device details in the Google Admin console show the device’s upgrade type, distinguishing a ChromeOS device bundled with ChromeOS Enterprise Upgrade from a standalone device using ChromeOS Enterprise Upgrade. Chromebook Enterprise devices carry a bundled upgrade that remains associated with the device for its lifetime, while CEU licenses are standalone upgrades.

**Learn more:** [View ChromeOS device list and details](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/1698333?hl=en) · [About ChromeOS devices with bundled upgrades](https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/9773699?hl=en)

A global organization is rolling out ChromeOS devices to all users. Corporate policy requires that all web traffic be filtered through an existing enterprise solution so employees cannot access 1 million unauthorized websites. What should be configured to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: A “Network access control deny
A firewall rule to blocklist the URLs
A user policy enforcing the use of a web proxy.
A user policy to blocklist the URLs.

questions.explanation:
ChromeOS URL blocklists are intended for basic URL management; stronger large-scale web filtering should use a content-filtering web proxy.
